A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PooDLe research, and their main text and appendices support reliable matching. v2 has a clipped architecture illustration in Figure 3, but the corresponding method remains accessible through its text and equations.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and detection experiments, component and cropping ablations, subcrop simulations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and detection results and adds WT-Sem evaluations, additional baseline results, and revised cropping experiments.

M1.justification: The dense and pooled objectives, flow-informed subcrop sampling, spatial decoder, ResNet-50 backbone, and training procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. WT-Sem construction introduces an evaluation dataset, not a new PooDLe component.

E1.justification: v2 adds WT-Sem, an automatically labeled semantic segmentation benchmark covering Walking Tours footage and three additional validation videos from Rome, Torun, and Poznan. This substantially extends evaluation into the walking-video domain while retaining BDD100K, Cityscapes, and ADE20K.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MAE ViT-S pretrained on WTVenice and WTall, plus WTall-pretrained DINO ViT-S in the ADE20K comparison. Removing the fixed-pixel-density experiment also removes its comparisons with FlowE and single-objective variants. The principal BDD, Cityscapes, and ImageNet-pretrained comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: v2 reports 512 x 1024 crops for all ResNet baselines, changes DenseCL's Table 1 training budget from 800 to 100 epochs, and broadens PixPro setting selection. Section 4.4 replaces crop-range sweeps with truncated-Gaussian sampling across three resolutions and adds an eight-frame temporal stride. WT-Sem introduces a 25,910/6,170-frame training/validation split and batch-size-four finetuning.

E4.justification: The global-crop study is redesigned, while the fixed-pixel-density comparison and v1 Appendix G's ViT activation-collapse analysis are removed. v2 adds WT-Sem distribution analyses and a backbone computation-cost comparison. The component ablations and subcrop-area analysis remain; the latter is redisplayed as Table 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Appendix A's retained repeated frame sampling concerns data loading rather than independent experimental replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds WT-Sem results, including linear mIoU of 11.2 for WTall-pretrained PooDLe versus 7.8 for DoRA, alongside new baseline, cropping, and GFLOP results. DenseCL's Table 1 BDD linear mIoU changes from 21.3 to 24.2 under revised training settings; its appendix per-class row remains unchanged. Fixed-density and ViT-failure findings disappear. PooDLe's original BDD, Cityscapes, and ADE20K scores are retained.

T1.justification: The loss equations, decoder recurrence, grid-sampling rule, and class-group definitions are retained. Neither version introduces new theorems or proofs; the revised cropping studies are empirical rather than changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central unified-method and downstream-performance claims remain. v2 adds the introduction of WT-Sem as a contribution, foregrounds balanced class-wise representations, and removes v1's explicit contribution claim about maintaining pixel density and its broader crop/resolution robustness claim.

C2.justification: v2 removes the limitations discussion covering external-flow dependence, poor ViT performance, and shortcomings of random subcrops, together with the proposed explanation for ViT collapse. It adds the rationale for an in-distribution Walking Tours benchmark and an SDM computational-efficiency interpretation. The discussion of noisy unsupervised flow remains in the appendix.

D1.justification: Appendices A and D add WT-Sem video sources and licensing, two-second sampling, the OpenSeeD/Swin-L labeling pipeline, split sizes, and evaluation settings. The project-page address changes. Existing PooDLe implementation, optimizer, hardware, and training-time disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for OpenSeeD, Swin Transformer, COCO, and Objects365, while removing the original ViT reference and motion-prior references associated with deleted discussions. Section 2 refines its critique of prior methods, but the principal positioning around unified pooled and dense learning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, related-work discussion, and several results passages are extensively rewritten. Section 4.4 is reordered and condensed, the limitations subsection disappears, and the appendices are reorganized around new benchmark and computation-cost sections. Citation style and front matter also change to the ICLR format.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands to include WT-Sem; Figure 5 is redesigned; the subcrop plot becomes Table 5; and benchmark illustrations and a GFLOP table are added. The ViT-collapse visualization is removed, while retained appendix figures are relocated and renumbered. Reformatting also places Figure 3(b) and its caption below page 4's visible boundary in v2.

improvement.justification: WT-Sem, additional baselines, revised baseline settings, and computation-cost reporting broaden the evidence. However, v2 removes documented ViT failures and important limitations without reporting their resolution, drops the controlled pixel-density analysis, and clips a key architecture illustration. These changes improve evaluation breadth while reducing transparency and readability; the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
